To enable recovery of the compressed information, it further introduces a dual-branch architecture for joint chunk decompression and bit decoding, along with a hard-message sampling strategy to improve combinatorial coverage during decoder training. Extensive experiments on the Blender and LLFF datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of BitC-3DGS for high-capacity watermarking, achieving high message recovery accuracy and rendering fidelity. For example, it supports 128-bit message capacity with recovery accuracy comparable to that of 64-bit messages in recent state-of-the-art methods.

2605.29894.title: Train the Agent, Not the Expert: Learning to Harness Heterogeneous Experts for Multi-Turn Visual Reasoning
2605.29894.authors: Yaowu Fan, Tao Han, Dazhao Du, Andy J. Ma, Jia Wan
2605.29894.abstract: Recent advances in computer vision have produced powerful specialized models for detection, segmentation, counting, and other visual tasks. However, these models are typically optimized for isolated tasks, limiting their ability to support general-purpose visual intelligence, particularly when complex language understanding and dense small-object perception are required. We propose VisHarness, a trainable visual agent that decouples high-level perception, reasoning, and decision-making from low-level task execution. Rather than training a task-specific model, we train VisHarness to harness a set of carefully designed heterogeneous visual experts. This paradigm preserves the agent's general intelligence while leveraging the precision of specialized visual experts for specific tasks. With only lightweight training, VisHarness learns a generalizable policy for harnessing visual experts, enabling it to solve fundamental vision tasks in diverse complex scenarios through multi-turn interactions with these experts. To enable efficient on-policy reinforcement learning in a live environment, we introduce dynamic visual memory archiving to reduce the visual-token overhead that rapidly accumulates during multi-turn interactions with visual experts. Experiments on four representative benchmarks spanning reasoning segmentation, generalized referring expression segmentation, dense small-object detection, and referring expression counting show that VisHarness substantially outperforms existing general-purpose models and is competitive with or superior to task-specific models. Our code, model weights, and training data are publicly available at https://github.com/fyw1999/VisHarness.

2605.31116.title: NTR: Neural Token Reconstruction for Scene Token Bottleneck in End-to-End Driving
2605.31116.authors: Jiahui Li, Jiawei Sun, Zixiang Ren, Ming Liu, Jiamin Shi, Ruiteng Zhao, Zhiyang Liu, Liying Liu, Zuoguan Wang, Kaidi Yang
2605.31116.abstract: Recent perception-free end-to-end (E2E) autonomous driving methods bypass explicit perception outputs by compressing dense image patch tokens into compact scene tokens for downstream trajectory generation and scoring. While these scene tokens form a compact visual bottleneck for the planner, they receive supervision solely from the planning objective, providing limited constraints on the encoded visual information. To address this limitation, we introduce Neural Token Reconstruction (NTR), a representation learning framework to directly constrain the compact scene-token bottleneck in perception-free driving. NTR introduces a self-distillation masked latent reconstruction objective that reconstructs masked patch-level latent features using only compact scene tokens as reconstruction memory. This forces reconstruction gradients to pass exclusively through the scene-token bottleneck, encouraging scene tokens to preserve richer and less redundant visual representations for planning. We further introduce semantic priors derived from foundation-model annotations as a weak semantic interface biasing reconstruction targets toward driving-related structures without introducing explicit perception heads. All auxiliary reconstruction components are removed at inference time, leaving the deployed planner unchanged. NTR achieves state-of-the-art performance on three public autonomous driving benchmarks, including 8.0461 RFS on Waymo E2E and 94.1 PDMS / 90.9 EPDMS on NavSim1&2. The learned scene tokens exhibit lower pairwise redundancy and higher effective rank, indicating that effective bottleneck supervision improves both compact visual representation learning and planning performance.

2606.03837.title: Where Do We (Not) Need Temporal Context in Low-Resource Video Task Adaptation?
2606.03837.authors: Luc P. J. Str\"ater, Hazel Doughty
2606.03837.abstract: Parameter-efficient finetuning (PEFT) and probing enable adaptation of foundation models using only a small number of trainable parameters. This makes these techniques attractive for video understanding where annotation and computation are expensive. However, video PEFT has focused on adapting image-pretrained models, while standard PEFT methods can also be applied to video representations. These settings are rarely compared and both confine temporal reasoning to a single component of the model, leaving open how temporal context should be distributed across backbone, PEFT, and probe. In this work, we provide a systematic study of model adaptation strategies for video understanding. We evaluate methods across appearance-focused, motion-focused and spatially dense settings, with a particular emphasis on scenarios with limited data where parameter efficiency is most beneficial. Our results provide new insights into PEFT and probing across task types and demonstrate the importance of temporal context allocation for effective video adaptation.

2606.05506.title: Robust Scene Transfer for PointGoal Navigation via Privileged Sensor Guided Contrastive Learning
2606.05506.authors: Amirhossein Zhalehmehrabi, Tiziano Tezze, Alberto Castellini, Alessandro Farinelli
2606.05506.abstract: We propose a sensor-guided adaptive contrastive learning framework for visual representation learning in PointGoal navigation. During training, privileged LiDAR sensing guides the contrastive objective through a geometry-aware similarity metric and adaptive temperature scaling, encouraging visual embeddings to capture navigation-relevant structure rather than scene-specific appearance. The resulting encoder is pretrained independently, frozen, and used as the perceptual backbone for reinforcement learning, decoupling representation learning from policy optimization. We further introduce a cross-stage domain mismatch between representation pretraining and policy learning to suppress environment-specific shortcuts and promote reliance on task-relevant features. Extensive experiments in high-fidelity simulation demonstrate that our approach significantly improves policy-level scene transfer across diverse indoor and outdoor environments. At deployment, the agent relies only on monocular RGB observations together with standard task-related inputs such as goal position and proprioceptive signals, without access to LiDAR or other privileged sensors. Our method outperforms large pretrained vision models and standard contrastive baselines under severe appearance and semantic shifts. We also release a multimodal dataset to support future research on privileged-guided visual representation learning for navigation. The code is available at:

2606.10522.title: GUI-AC: Enhancing Continual Learning in GUI Agents
2606.10522.authors: Can Lin, Wenjun Yang, Tao Feng, Hangjie Yuan, Dan Zhang, Yifan Zhu, Zhonghong Ou, Wen Chen, Jian Wu
2606.10522.abstract: Graphical User Interfaces (GUIs) serve as the dominant medium for human-computer interaction, yet building GUI agents that generalize across the vast diversity of real-world interface environments, with the same flexibility and robustness that humans naturally exhibit, remains unsolved. Notably, GUI data are inherently non-stationary: the continual emergence of previously unseen interface instances (e.g., novel domains and resolutions) induces persistent distribution shifts, significantly impeding the continual learning of existing GUI agents. Reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT) has attracted considerable attention as a promising approach. Nevertheless, RFT exhibits pronounced instability in its grounding capability, where rollout outcomes are highly imbalanced and fixed clipping can suppress valuable exploration. More importantly, policy probability alone does not reveal the semantic role of a grounding prediction. To address these challenges, we propose GUI-AC, a continual RFT framework that jointly characterizes grounding rollouts through advantage and policy probability. This yields a four-region view of grounding behavior and enables targeted optimization of Exploration and Overconfidence. GUI-AC further introduces grounding certainty to support two core mechanisms: (i) Adaptive Advantage, which strengthens the negative correction for overconfident grounding failures; and (ii) Dynamic Clipping, which relaxes the upper clipping bound for exploratory grounding rollouts. Extensive experiments show that GUI-AC consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. Code is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/GUI-AC-Code.

2606.11846.title: SheafStain: Sheaf-Theoretic Schr\"odinger Bridge for Spatially and Biologically Coherent Virtual Staining
2606.11846.authors: Hyeongyeol Lim, Hongjun Yoon, Eunjin Jang, Daeky Jeong, Won June Cho, Hwamin Lee
2606.11846.abstract: Current virtual staining approaches offer the potential for time- and cost-efficient biomarker quantification in cancer diagnostics and prognostics. However, patch-wise inference for gigapixel whole-slide images fails to maintain spatial continuity, yielding artifacts that cause catastrophic mismatches with ground-truth images. Although pathology Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) offer rich representations, their self-attention causes varying global contexts to produce inconsistent embeddings for the same physical region. We formalize and validate this "context contamination" as a sheaf-theoretic problem where these embeddings form a presheaf whose sections disagree on overlaps, so no global section restricts to them. To address this, we propose SheafStain, a new approach that reinterprets VFM features as sheaf-like sections for spatially and biologically coherent virtual staining. Specifically, SheafStain integrates class and patch tokens into a Schr\"odinger Bridge framework as sheaf-like sections. While the class token anchors biological consistency, patch tokens form a per-position spatial map. A feature space from a single VFM encoder pretrained on Hematoxylin \& Eosin and Immunohistochemistry supervises both input conditioning and output stain alignment. Departing from prior work that evaluates on isolated $256 \times 256$ patches and either random-crops or resizes the $1024 \times 1024$ ground truth, we translate at $256 \times 256$ and evaluate on the stitched $1024 \times 1024$ outputs across HER2, ER, PR, and Ki-67. SheafStain demonstrates promising results against six prior methods while mitigating patch-boundary stitching artifacts. Code is available at https://github.com/deepnoid-ai/SheafStain.

2606.13312.title: MEGMAG: Micro-Expression Generation via MAGnification
2606.13312.abstract: Facial micro-expressions are subtle, short-lived facial movements that reveal genuine human emotions. Despite the large advances in facial expression synthesis and animation, realistic micro-expressions remain challenging due to scarce annotated data and the extremely subtle nature of their motion. Existing dedicated micro-expression methods therefore often struggle with generation quality, robustness, and generalization. We present MEGMAG, a transferable framework for micro-expression generation via magnification that enables pretrained facial animation models to generate realistic micro-expressions without modifying or fine-tuning their backbones. The key idea is to transform subtle micro-expression dynamics into the domain of regular facial expressions, where pretrained animation models can effectively capture and transfer facial motion. A learnable Magnification Module amplifies subtle micro-expression dynamics, enabling a frozen facial animation backbone to transfer the amplified motion to a source identity without altering its original architecture or parameters. A DeMagnification Module then attenuates the generated motion to recover realistic micro-expression characteristics. This design allows MEGMAG to leverage diverse off-the-shelf facial animation models while remaining architecture-agnostic and fully transferable across backbones.

2606.14534.title: A Lightweight Fiducial-Based Pipeline for 3D Hyperspectral Mapping of ex-vivo Lumpectomy Specimens
2606.14534.authors: Anna Bicchi, Alberto Rota, Leonardo Passoni, Nicola Ancellotti, Andrea Peroni, Lorenzo Vinco, Dario Polli, Elena De Momi
2606.14534.abstract: Hyperspectral Imaging (HSI) is a promising modality for intraoperative assessment of resection margins in Breast-Conserving Surgery (BCS), but its clinical translation requires aligning the inherently 2D spectral information onto the 3D shape of the excised tissue so that suspicious regions can be precisely localized for targeted follow-up. We present a fully automated, calibration-free pipeline that produces a 3D hyperspectral point cloud of an ex-vivo lumpectomy specimen from a set of consumer-camera RGB images and a single top-down HSI acquisition. The 3D geometry is reconstructed with a deep-learning Structure-from-Motion backbone, stabilized in a metric reference frame by a custom bundle adjustment that enforces consistency on the corners of four ArUco markers placed around the specimen. The HSI cube is then registered to the reconstruction without recovering the HSI camera pose: the markers, visible in both modalities, define 16 corner correspondences that drive a planar homography, and 3D coordinates are recovered by lookup on an orthographically rendered depth map. Evaluated on two ex-vivo lumpectomy specimens, the pipeline achieves a median 3D registration error below 1~mm and a 2D reprojection error below 0.02 mm, with a total per-specimen processing time under 4 minutes on accelerated hardware. These results support the feasibility of integrating HSI-guided spatial localization into intraoperative margin assessment workflows for breast-conserving surgery.

2606.17342.title: Learning a Maximum Entropy Model for Visual Textures using Diffusion
2606.17342.abstract: Visual textures -- spatially homogeneous image regions containing repeated elements (e.g. a field of grass, the bark of a tree) -- are ubiquitous in visual scenes and provide important cues for recognizing and analyzing materials, surface geometry and objects. A number of existing texture models extract essential statistics from a single texture image, and can then generate high-quality samples that are visually similar to the original by matching these statistics. However, their statistics are either hand-designed or based on a network pretrained for another purpose (e.g., object recognition). Here, we develop the first principled method for unsupervised learning of a set of statistics that are used to constrain a maximum entropy probability model for texture. We leverage methods developed for generative diffusion models to derive training and sampling procedures, and compare these to the traditional method of sampling via matching the statistics. Despite the compactness of our trained model (512 statistics), it generates texture images whose quality is as good as or better than the current state-of-the-art model (~177k statistics), both visually and by quantitative perceptual scoring using DreamSim. Finally, we show that images generated from parameters lying along a line between the parameter vectors corresponding to two different reference textures are homogeneous textures with features that smoothly transition between those of the two references.

2606.23503.title: UniverSat: Resolution- and Modality-Agnostic Transformers for Earth Observation
2606.23503.authors: Yohann Perron, Guillaume Astruc, Nicolas Gonthier, Clement Mallet, Loic Landrieu
2606.23503.abstract: Vision Transformers (ViT) dominate computer vision. However, their reliance on rigid patch projectors hinders transfer to Earth Observation (EO), where input modalities, scales, and resolutions vary widely. We introduce UniverSat, a ViT-style backbone built around a Universal Patch Encoder that maps patches from arbitrary spatial, spectral, and temporal resolutions, and from both optical and non-optical sensors, into a shared embedding space with a shared set of weights. This enables training a single model on heterogeneous multimodal corpora via self-supervision, yielding robust, sensor-agnostic spatial features. We validate this approach with strong results across classification and segmentation on standard EO benchmarks from GeoBench, PANGEABench, and SpectralEarth. Our code and models are available at https://github.com/gastruc/UniverSat.

2606.24153.title: Differential Unfolding: Efficient Reconstruction for Video Snapshot Compressive Imaging
2606.24153.authors: Yin-Ping Zhao, Muyuan Zhang, Jiaxi Li, Jiancheng Zhang, Haijin Zeng, Xuelong Li
2606.24153.abstract: Although Deep Unfolding Networks (DUNs) are predominant in Video Snapshot Compressive Imaging (SCI), they are still limited by a uniform design philosophy. The existing approaches stack high-complexity priors with the same structure repeatedly, neglecting the fact that the optimization paths gradually converge to a nearly static state. As a consequence, representation stagnation occurs, and much computational cost is wasted on small feature updates. To solve this inefficiency, we propose Differential Unfolding (DU), a heterogeneous framework that substitutes repeated work with a periodic schedule of heavy and lightweight stages. The core of DU is the Differential Evolutionary Framework (DEF), which divides the unfolding procedure into two complementary roles: structural anchoring and differential evolution. In this method, high-parameter general stages are used sparsely to form high-fidelity feature foundations. On the other hand, lightweight differential stages use a Differential Representation Prior (DRP) to pass on and refine these foundational features by a differential mechanism. By integrating Differential Representation Attention (DRA) for evolving attention maps and a Differential Modulated FFN (DM-FFN) for feature rectification, DRP effectively models cross-stage variations with minimal overhead. By concentrating high-capacity computation on the sparsely-scheduled general stages and delegating incremental refinement to the lightweight differential stages, DU achieves a superior trade-off between accuracy and efficiency. Extensive experiments show that DU-9stg achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction quality, while DU-5stg surpasses all compared methods with the fewest parameters and FLOPs; compared with the unfolding method DADUN, DU-9stg needs about half the parameters and a quarter of the FLOPs. Code: https://github.com/Muyuan-Zhang/DU

2606.29976.title: Learning Motion-Expressive 4D Gaussian Representations from Monocular Videos with Flow Splatting
2606.29976.abstract: Reconstructing dynamic 3D scenes from monocular videos remains challenging because limited observations provide insufficient motion constraints. Conventional 4D Gaussian representations model spatiotemporal appearance efficiently, but the restricted temporal evolution of each primitive makes complex nonlinear dynamics difficult to represent compactly. We propose a motion-expressive 4D Gaussian representation with time-varying means and covariances. By analytically differentiating Gaussian trajectories, we obtain Gaussian velocities and introduce Flow Splatting to render optical flow while accounting for camera motion, enabling dense motion supervision. This formulation jointly models scene appearance and motion within a unified set of 4D Gaussian primitives. We further introduce an initialization strategy based on the sampling theorem and a velocity consistency regularizer to stabilize optimization. Experiments on DAVIS and NVIDIA Dynamic Scenes demonstrate a favorable trade-off between reconstruction quality and efficiency under challenging monocular settings.

2606.30097.title: CylindTrack: Depth-Aware Cylindrical Motion Modeling for Panoramic Multi-Object Tracking in Mobile Robots
2606.30097.authors: Buyin Deng, Kai Luo, Lingxin Huang, Xinqi Liu, Fei Cheng, Hang Zheng, Liming Yin, Kailun Yang
2606.30097.abstract: Maintaining consistent target identities and observation histories is essential for mobile robot perception. Panoramic Multi-Object Tracking (MOT) benefits from broad visual coverage but must address coordinate discontinuities at the equirectangular image seam and fluctuations in relative-depth estimates. Such fluctuations can undermine depth-aware association, highlighting the need for temporally consistent depth cues. We propose CylindTrack, a depth-aware cylindrical tracking-by-detection framework that jointly models panoramic topology and temporal depth consistency. Depth-Temporal Trajectory Modeling (DTM) maintains instance depth and its rate of change as filtered trajectory states. Spherical Spatio-Temporal Consistency Learning (SSTC) combines a Temporal Mixer with Spherical Geometry-aware Attention to refine depth-aware representations. A Topology-Aware Cylindrical Motion Model (TCMM) represents horizontal motion in an unwrapped angular state and incorporates periodic overlap, angular consistency, and filtered depth cues into association. Experiments on QuadTrack and JRDB demonstrate improved identity consistency and trajectory continuity, with HOTA scores of 33.67 and 31.12 and IDF1 scores of 40.45 and 34.33, respectively. The framework processes 28.56 and 21.34 frames per second, respectively, on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 GPU under the reported evaluation settings. These results support persistent panoramic multi-object tracking for mobile robot perception. The source code will be released at https://github.com/warriordby/CylindTrack.

2607.09164.title: What Pixels Are Enough? SEAMS: Sufficiency Saliency via MSE-Preservation Soft-Masks
2607.09164.authors: Magdalena Tr\k{e}dowicz, {\L}ukasz Struski, Arkadiusz Lewicki, Karolina Pachota, Andrzej Grudzie\'n, Mateusz Jag{\l}a, Jacek Tabor
2607.09164.abstract: Saliency maps are most useful when they identify the image regions that are sufficient to preserve a model's behaviour. We introduce SEAMS, a sufficiency-based saliency method that directly optimises a soft mask using a preservation objective. Given a frozen differentiable model output, such as a class probability, CLS embedding, or token representation, SEAMS searches for a compact mask that preserves the selected output. The approach relies on a simple optimisation framework based on soft masks, a learnable budget, and a three-way image composite generated entirely from the query image. As a result, it requires no auxiliary distractor dataset, architecture-specific attribution mechanism, or differentiable top-k relaxation. Experiments with frozen ViT-S/16 and ConvNeXt models show that the same optimisation pipeline can generate object-level, class-conditioned, and token-level explanations by changing only the preserved target. The resulting masks are compact, interpretable, stable across random initialisations, and competitive on insertion and deletion benchmarks. Our results also indicate that different architectures often rely on different sufficient evidence while achieving similar preservation fidelity, highlighting the architecture-dependent nature of visual explanations.

2607.12052.title: Representation and Reference Selection in Training-Free Synthetic Image Attribution
2607.12052.authors: Meiling Li, Pietro Bongini, Benedetta Tondi, Mauro Barni
2607.12052.abstract: Synthetic image attribution aims at identifying the generator responsible for a given AI-generated image. Training-free reference-based attribution methods are easily scalable, since newly emerging generators can be incorporated by adding source-specific references rather than retraining a task-specific classifier. Their performance depends on two coupled factors: the representation space used for comparison and the way source-specific references are constructed. However, the interaction between these two factors remains largely unexplored. In this paper, we provide a controlled analysis of this interaction using references and off-the-shelf pretrained representations. We study representations extracted from different layers of CLIP and DINOv2, along with three reference selection strategies with varying semantic constraints: arbitrary, semantically aligned, and resynthesis-based references. Our results show that attribution accuracy generally peaks at intermediate representation levels, indicating that source-discriminative cues are more accessible before strong semantic abstraction dominates. We further show that intermediate representations are not completely semantically neutral, making reference selection critical: semantically constrained references reduce query-reference mismatch and improve attribution, especially under limited reference budgets. Resynthesis is useful in low-reference regimes, while semantically aligned references provide a better accuracy-cost trade-off when a moderate-sized reference pool is available. Our findings show that training-free reference-based attribution should be understood as the interaction between where images are compared, how the reference set is constructed, and how many references are available. Code and datasets are available at https://github.com/meiling-fdu/RefPrint.

2607.13361.title: Detector Confidence Signals Presence Rather Than Occlusion in Cluttered Manipulation
2607.13361.abstract: Detector confidence is often used to decide whether a robot needs another view of a target. We test this signal against detector-free visibility from geometry segmentation. In controlled clutter, Grounding DINO confidence remains nearly constant as target visibility falls from all scenes to one in eight. OWLv2 and SAM 3 retain positive correlations with visibility, but all three detectors lose target-instance localization under heavy occlusion. Grounding DINO reports a hidden target present in about nine of ten scenes by detecting same-category distractors. Consequently, confidence understates the benefit of additional views ($8$ versus $88$ percentage points). In a $40$-scene localization comparison, additional-view selection and fusion increase target localizability from $5\%$ to $100\%$. Experiments cover nine categories, two simulators, and real video. On DAVIS, confidence correlates positively with visible area, yet $99\%$ of occluded frames yield a detection and $94\%$ of those detections miss the tracked target. These results distinguish category presence from target visibility and motivate target-grounded evaluation of active perception.

2607.25276.title: FunnelAL: Retrieve-then-Rank Active Learning for Single-Class Discovery
2607.25276.authors: Reihaneh Rostami (RAIC Labs), Brian Goodwin (RAIC Labs)
2607.25276.abstract: We present FunnelAL, a retrieve-then-rank active learning system for single-class discovery, which adapts the multi-stage funnel architecture of industrial recommender systems to data annotation. Starting from one positive and one negative example, FunnelAL repeats three stages: (1) embedding-based retrieval that narrows the corpus to a candidate set, (2) a ranking stage that exploits a learned ranker (RankNet) and, once batch precision falls, mixes in committee-based exploration (QBC), and (3) the annotator's labels, which refine both stages for the next round. We evaluate on five datasets, three benchmarks and two large corpora of up to 2.7 million images, each with two different pretrained encoders, DINOv2 and CLIP. With clean labels and DINOv2, FunnelAL has the best mean rank over the five datasets, and with CLIP it shares the best rank with its ablation Funnel-RankNet. On the three benchmarks it discovers positives significantly faster than the classical and uncertainty-based baselines and than PF-MA, and no significant difference from PF-MA's final F1 was detected. With DINOv2, no significant difference from SEALS's active-search mode (most-likely-positive selection) was detected on most datasets. With CLIP, FunnelAL discovers significantly faster than it on three of the five. On iNaturalist's working set of 2.15 million images FunnelAL selects eight times faster than the neighborhood baselines as we implemented them (SEALS in both its modes and AnchorAL, which select only among the nearest neighbors of labeled items). There, PF-MA and uncertainty sampling, which label items near the decision boundary across the whole pool, reach a higher F1 under our evaluation protocol. Under 10% annotator label noise it has a higher F1 than every baseline on three of the five datasets with DINOv2 and on all five with CLIP, and SEALS's active-search mode is more robust at higher rates.

2607.26232.title: Image Forgery Detection under Generative and Composited Background Replacement: A Benchmark with Processing-Matched Controls
2607.26232.abstract: Consumer tools can now keep the subject of a photograph and replace, relight or edit everything behind it. Such edits place genuine people and objects in scenes they were never in, yet involve processing--resampling, harmonization, diffusion autoencoders--that also occurs in benign workflows. We introduce BG-REAL, a benchmark of 25,624 images built from 2,485 Open Images photographs with a dominant subject and real donor scenes. Each recipient is edited by donor compositing, learned harmonization, generative background inpainting, foreground-conditioned relighting and local background edits, and is paired with authentic controls that share the processing but not the semantic edit; all images of a recipient share file format and JPEG quality. Three generators (including FLUX.1 Fill), scene categories and subject classes are held out. Seven detectors published between 2022 and 2026 reach zero-shot AUROCs of at most 0.745 and have no useful operating point: manipulation localisers mark the preserved subject instead of the replaced background, and a detector of AI-generated images flags most authentic images passed through a diffusion autoencoder. After fine-tuning, the strongest detectors reach an AUROC of about 0.95, while re-implemented background-forgery detectors remain below 0.80. Controls show that full-background replacements by the training generators are detected from the edit itself, whereas local edits and SDXL and FLUX edits remain hard, and that full-background localisation largely reduces to subject segmentation. A model-agnostic training objective that uses the controls improves detection on unseen subjects for one detector and on local edits for another without changing in-distribution accuracy. The data are released.

2607.27982.title: ViP-Rig: Visual-Prompted Controllable Rigging
2607.27982.authors: Zihan Qin, Mingze Sun, Yifan Mao, Jialei Xu, Jingfeng Guo, Changrong Hu, Wenbo Zhao, Junjun Jiang, Xianming Liu
2607.27982.abstract: Rigging is inherently task-dependent because the same mesh may require different skeletons and deformation behaviors across animation tasks. In practice, artists often inspect an initial rig and repeatedly edit its skeletal structure and deformation behavior to meet specific animation requirements. Existing automatic methods primarily generate a plausible rig from geometry, offering limited explicit control over the resulting skeleton and deformation behavior. In this work, we present ViP-Rig, a visual-prompted framework that supports both prompt-first rigging and result-guided editing by injecting features extracted from user-drawn or edited 2D skeletal and rigidity prompts into frozen pretrained backbones. Specifically, ViP-Rig consists of two stages, Skeleton Generation and Skinning Prediction. In the first stage, the skeletal sketch is processed by the Dense-to-Compact Visual Prompt Encoding to produce compact, fixed-length conditioning tokens. The resulting tokens are injected into a frozen pretrained autoregressive generator through gated adapters to control joint placement and branching structure while preserving the generator's geometric prior. In the second stage, the rigidity map is processed using the same visual encoding design, while the pretrained skinning backbone remains frozen. The resulting tokens are symmetrically injected into the point and joint streams to modulate point-joint compatibility and the resulting skinning weights. Experiments on Articulation-XL2.0 and zero-shot evaluation on ModelsResource show that ViP-Rig more accurately recovers target skeletons and skinning weights than geometry-conditioned baselines under prompt-guided evaluation. Qualitative results further demonstrate explicit and localized control in both prompt-first rigging and result-guided editing.

2608.08285.title: Ego-OSCAR: Egocentric Open source Stereo CAptuRe System
2608.08285.authors: Senthil Palanisamy, Satpal Singh Rathore, Pratyush Kumar Patnaik, Shubhanshu Khatana, Gunjan Paul, Abhishek Anand
2608.08285.abstract: Egocentric vision has scaled its corpora far faster than its instruments. Calibrated stereo rigidly coupled to a synchronized inertial stream is not new; research-grade headsets deliver it. What does not exist is an open version: those platforms are closed products a third party cannot build or extend, and the consumer cameras used elsewhere are monocular and rolling-shutter. The instrument is the least reproducible part of an otherwise open pipeline. We present our system, an open-hardware head-mounted capture platform, at a complete bill of materials under USD 200 in commodity parts and 3D prints. It pairs a hardware-synchronized global-shutter stereo camera with a 6-axis IMU, an embedded Linux SBC for on-device encoding, and a real-time microcontroller that bridges the camera and inertial clock domains to a residual of 700 microseconds and watchdogs the recording against silent failure. We release the full stack alongside the device: CAD, firmware, recording and time-synchronization tooling, and our corpus, roughly 550 hours of stereo video over 1,462 sessions and 25 contributors, every device shipping its own stereo calibration. The corpus ships with model-predicted annotation layers rather than raw video alone, including per-frame 3D hand reconstructions spanning essentially the whole timeline; these are automatic predictions, not human-verified ground truth, and we report them as such. We characterize the instrument along sensor fidelity, data utility, and six months of distributed field deployment. Our system is not the highest fidelity egocentric rig; it is the cheapest one a reader of this paper can reproduce, and the only corpus here that others can extend rather than only consume.

2608.23927.title: GlanceWAM: Sparse Test-Time Imagination for World-Action Models
2608.23927.authors: Linhan Wang, Zijian An, Mingyuan Zhang, Chen Dai, Yi Xu, Can Cui, Jiayan Wang, Zichong Yang, Yinlin Chen, Lifeng Zhou, Chang-Tien Lu
2608.23927.abstract: Video generative models provide rich physical priors for robot learning, yet existing world-action models (WAMs) face a fundamental trade-off: synchronous video generation at control rate is latency-prohibitive, while abandoning test-time visual imagination sacrifices task success. We show that visual imagination achieves both real-time inference and superior success rates when generated asynchronously off the critical path and consumed directly in latent space. We introduce GlanceWAM, which decouples imagination from control on a single shared video DiT backbone: an asynchronous proposer glances ahead on a slow clock to imagine a single lookahead frame seconds into the future in the background, while an action head decodes action chunks at control rate (48 ms) purely in latent space without blocking. Enabled by a non-interfering attention mask that isolates video representations and staleness-robust horizon training that accommodates asynchronous lookahead aging, GlanceWAM breaks the speed-success dilemma. Trained purely on demonstrations, it attains 72.2% on the 24-task RoboCasa kitchen benchmark (vs. 67.1% for synchronous Cosmos Policy) and 99.0% on LIBERO while cutting per-chunk control latency 24x relative to synchronous world-action models (48 ms on one A100). In single-arm and bimanual real-robot manipulation, it achieves higher average success than $\pi_{0.5}$ without any robot-data pretraining. Code is available at https://github.com/linhanwang/GlanceWAM and real-robot videos at https://linhanwang.github.io/glancewam/.

2608.26686.title: Domain-Specific Self-Supervised Representation Learning for Retinal Fundus Classification
2608.26686.abstract: Annotated medical images remain scarce and costly to obtain, which motivates self-supervised learning (SSL). We present a controlled empirical study of two SSL frameworks, SimSiam and SimCLR, for retinal fundus classification, asking whether retina-specific augmentations (Graham's local-mean subtraction and CLAHE) improve representations beyond standard augmentation and grayscale conversion. ResNet-18 backbones are pretrained on 48K unlabeled fundus images and evaluated by linear probing and fine-tuning on EDID (multi-disease) and RetinaMNIST (DR grading). On EDID, grayscale conversion accounts for most of SimSiam's linear-probe gain, and Graham or CLAHE add little on top of it. After fine-tuning, SimSiam with Graham+Gray exceeds an ImageNet-supervised baseline on RetinaMNIST (+3.0 accuracy points) but only matches it on EDID. Retina-specific augmentation therefore helps inconsistently and should be validated per SSL method and task.

2608.27562.title: VidParse: Online Parsing of Egocentric Procedures Like a Pro
2608.27562.authors: Anubhav Gupta, Archit Kambhamettu, Vatsal Agarwal, Pulkit Kumar, Abhinav Shrivastava
2608.27562.abstract: Translating continuous, noisy egocentric video streams into discrete, temporally ordered action steps is fraught with visual challenges. Heavy ego-motion, transient occlusions, and the high intra-class variability of unscripted human-object interactions cause standard frame-level online temporal models to struggle, often resulting in severe over-segmentation and structural collapse. To bridge the gap between unstable low-level perception and high-level procedural logic, we present VidParse, an online, training-free framework that treats activity understanding as a graph-constrained inference problem. Rather than relying on learned temporal filters, we dynamically identify semantic transitions using a temporal similarity matrix over manipulation-anchored features, which are extracted from frozen foundation models to prioritize foreground hand-object interactions. A beam search decoder then leverages an induced procedural task graph to explicitly enforce valid action transitions and prune impossible trajectories. By anchoring robust visual segments to hard procedural constraints, our approach preserves long-range state transitions and achieves up to a 10x improvement in complex multi-step parsing accuracy over strong online baselines, all without requiring a single gradient update.

2608.28665.title: Understanding Temporal Semantic Stability in Open-Vocabulary UAV Perception through Metric 3D Fusion
2608.28665.abstract: Recent open-vocabulary segmentation models have significantly advanced semantic perception for UAVs, for aerial and remote-sensing imagery, yet predictions from moving platforms can remain temporally inconsistent across repeated observations of the same physical scene. While semantic segmentation is typically evaluated on single images, temporal reliability remains less explored despite its importance for long-horizon robotic perception. In this work, we investigate temporal semantic stability by associating frame-wise predictions with persistent world-space locations through metric 3D fusion. We introduce a voxel-level evaluation framework that jointly characterises final semantic agreement, Semantic Belief Drift (SBD), Observation Persistence (OP), and semantic uncertainty from accumulated evidence. Experiments on UAVid-3D-Scenes reveal substantial frame-wise semantic variation and show that high aggregate world-space agreement can overstate temporal stability when many locations have limited repeated-observation support. Persistence-stratified analysis shows that recurrent voxels expose substantially greater semantic disagreement, while higher-persistence voxels exhibit lower direct consecutive semantic-evidence divergence. This behaviour is observed across two segmentation backbones and remains consistent under variations in voxel resolution, geometric association, and temporal sampling density. Overall, conditions that reduce world-space recurrence can increase apparent aggregate stability, demonstrating that semantic consistency must be interpreted together with observation support. Our findings establish observation persistence as an essential conditioning variable for evaluating long-horizon semantic reliability and provide a framework for analysing temporal semantic behaviour beyond image-level prediction.

2609.05912.title: FreeTransformSR: Efficient Lightweight Image Super-Resolution via Free Low-Rank Learnable Transform
2609.05912.abstract: Single image super-resolution aims to reconstruct high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs. This paper proposes FreeTransformSR, a novel lightweight super-resolution network based on a channel-wise free low-rank learnable transform. The transform learns task-adaptive basis functions in a data-driven manner, enabling adaptive feature modulation with minimal parameter overhead. To further enhance high-frequency detail recovery, we introduce a local feature modulation branch that complements transform-domain processing with depthwise convolution. In addition, a soft complexity adaptive module dynamically fuses the outputs of local convolution and window self-attention branches through a lightweight gating network, adaptively adjusting the fusion ratio based on regional texture characteristics. An adaptive intensity modulation strategy is also incorporated to adjust transform-domain response strength at the sample level, enabling the network to dynamically adjust processing intensity according to input features. Extensive experiments on five benchmark datasets demonstrate that FreeTransformSR achieves competitive PSNR/SSIM performance with significantly fewer parameters and FLOPs. Specifically, FreeTransformSR achieves 32.41 dB on BSD100 x2 and 27.00 dB on Urban100 x4 with only 595K parameters, while delivering faster inference speed than competing methods, making it well-suited for deployment in resource-constrained scenarios. Source code is available at: https://github.com/HJiLi/FreeTransformSR.

2609.11472.title: BridgeMatch: Conditional Transport Bridges in Matching Matrix Space for 3D Deformable Registration
2609.11472.authors: Qianliang Wu, Yaqing Ding, Guangwei Gao, Weiping Ding, Jin Xie, Jian Yang
2609.11472.abstract: Non-rigid point cloud registration depends on accurate correspondences under deformation and partial visibility. Existing coarse-to-fine methods use coarse matches to select regions for fine matching, but incorrect selection can remove valid correspondences before refinement. We introduce \paper, a conditional transport framework that connects coarse correspondence estimation to high-resolution matching. A diffusion model first estimates a coarse matching matrix. We lift the complete estimate to a fine-level source matrix and refine its scores with a geometry-conditioned bridge. We consider two bridge formulations: a deterministic endpoint-parameterized flow and a stochastic paired Brownian bridge with endpoint and noise prediction. At each step, the current matrix provides an alignment for the next prediction. Both models reuse backbone features throughout inference. Experiments on 4DMatch and 4DLoMatch show improved correspondence and non-rigid registration accuracy. The models also transfer to CAPE and DeepDeform without target-domain training. Ablations examine the roles of candidate coverage, source initialization, and refinement budget.

2609.18465.title: GeoCond: A Conditioning-Aware Reliability Adapter for Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction
2609.18465.authors: David Ahmedt-Aristizabal, Mohammad Ali Armin, Russell Tsuchida, Lars Petersson
2609.18465.abstract: Feed-forward 3D foundation models such as VGGT predict cameras, depth, and point maps in a single pass, but can fail silently under low overlap, low parallax, and extreme relative rotation. Stratified analyses over these factors show that these failures are governed by geometric conditioning and are poorly captured by native aleatoric confidence. We introduce GeoCond, a lightweight reliability adapter for frozen feed-forward 3D backbones. GeoCond reads geometric conditioning cues and the backbone's own stability signals and outputs pose-level uncertainty and a refinement gate. During training, it can be supervised by frame-permutation orbit variance, ground-truth pose error when labels are available, or cycle residuals from unlabelled independent pose graphs. At inference, the default head requires only one backbone pass and a small MLP. On VGGT, GeoCond improves out-of-distribution (OOD) AUSE (area under the sparsification-error curve; lower is better) from $0.32$ to $0.20$ over native confidence on held-out outdoor scenes (and to $0.21$ when trained on indoor data only) and avoids the collapse caused by applying bundle adjustment uniformly, without improving on feed-forward poses there. For three of six backbones, cycle-distilled variants provide a ground-truth-free adaptation route, including cases where permutation variance vanishes on equivariant models. The same reliability signal supports gated refinement, pose-graph weighting, calibration, curation, and capture decisions. Reliable feed-forward 3D reconstruction requires not only predicting geometry, but also knowing when that geometry should be trusted.

2609.24850.title: Revisiting Multi-View Stereo: A Sequence-to-Sequence Formulation
2609.24850.authors: Aoxiang Fan, Corentin Dumery, Nicolas Talabot, Pascal Fua
2609.24850.abstract: Computing accurate geometry from multi-view images is a fundamental problem in computer vision. Recent feed-forward (FF) models jointly estimate 3D geometry and camera parameters, but they typically suffer from geometry distortion caused by reconstruction ambiguity, even when ground-truth camera parameters are supplied. In this paper, we study the multi-view stereo (MVS) problem with known camera parameters and propose a novel approach that bridges conventional MVS and FF methods. Rather than casting MVS as a sequence-to-one mapping that predicts depth only for a single reference view, we reformulate it as a sequence-to-sequence task, akin to FF models, that jointly predicts geometry for all input views. We introduce a global transformer-based architecture with two components that explicitly exploit camera-induced priors: ray-map embeddings that inject camera parameters into image patch tokens, making the transformer camera-aware, and a unified global cost volume that replaces conventional per-view cost volumes to jointly capture 3D structure across all views. Extensive experiments on multiple public benchmarks show our approach achieves state-of-the-art performance, surpassing both MVS and FF reconstruction baselines.

2609.27611.title: A generalizable structural brain MRI foundation model via dual-priority federated pretraining
2609.27611.authors: Zhen Yu, Yang Liu, Jianfeng Feng, Xiahai Zhuang, Qingchao Chen
2609.27611.abstract: Foundation models hold promise for generalizable analysis of structural brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans across diverse populations and imaging conditions. However, existing models typically rely on centralized pretraining using data pooled across cohorts, which is constrained by privacy and data-governance requirements. Moreover, larger cohorts can dominate optimization, underutilizing anatomical information from smaller cohorts and limiting generalization. Here we present BrainFedFM, a structural brain MRI foundation model federatively pretrained on 164,707 three-dimensional scans drawn from diverse real-world data distributions and organized across 42 federated sites. BrainFedFM uses dual-priority federated pretraining, in which spatial-priority masking emphasizes informative anatomical regions during local training, while site-priority aggregation adaptively weights contributions during global aggregation. Across 20 downstream datasets spanning 17 classification, regression and segmentation tasks, BrainFedFM achieved the state-of-the-art performance across seven foundation models, including four centralized models, while showing consistent advantages in classification and regression tasks and strong robustness under underrepresented populations and challenging imaging conditions. These findings demonstrate the generalizability of BrainFedFM and highlight federated pretraining as a practical strategy for developing neuroimaging foundation models from distributed data without pooling raw images.

2609.34183.title: CRF Loss is How Networks Should Learn Boundaries in Weakly Supervised Segmentation
2609.34183.abstract: Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation (WSSS) learns pixel-level predictions from image-level tags. Recent work focuses on improving coarse CAMs extracted from large vision-language models (commonly CLIP), but does little to improve their accuracy along segment boundaries. That job is instead delegated to a post-processing method like DenseCRF. However, because DenseCRF relies on low-level colour cues, it can flip correct labels to incorrect ones when neighbouring pixels share similar colours. SAM has recently been adopted as a natural alternative, yet it simply takes on DenseCRF's role as an intermediate "refinement" step that outputs one-hot pseudo-labels in prior work. By discarding the valuable uncertainty in CAMs, these one-hot pseudo-labels turn borderline errors into confidently wrong targets. Our key insight is that CAMs should supervise training alongside SAM boundaries, each through its own loss, rather than being fused together into a single hard target. Inspired by CRF potentials, we propose a framework that disentangles soft pseudo-labels as unary supervision and binary edge maps as pairwise supervision. We realize our framework in a single-stage model, DS-CRF, using CAMs from dino.txt and boundaries from SAM. DS-CRF sets a new state-of-the-art of 56.5% mIoU on MS COCO among training-based methods.

2609.34982.title: ActionUNet: Improving Robustness of VLA Models with Efficient Multi-scale Fine-tuning
2609.34982.authors: Di Zhu, Ziheng Yan, Fang Wan
2609.34982.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have shown great promise for robotic manipulation by mapping multi-modal semantics to physical actions. However, this mapping inherently struggles to align these coarse-grained semantics with fine-grained temporal execution. It leaves VLA models with limited generalization and insufficient robustness in cluttered environments. To overcome this issue, we propose ActionUNet, an efficient multi-scale fine-tuning framework that enhances pre-trained VLA models with minimal computational cost. ActionUNet first constructs a lightweight temporal U-Net within the temporal-aligned action feature space to fuse hierarchical structural priors, effectively bridging the scale gap between semantics and temporal executions. Recognizing that multi-scale modeling can disrupt microscopic temporal continuity and cause mechanical oscillations, ActionUNet then employs a conditional SIREN as a continuous action decoder. Equipped with explicit second-order smoothness constraints, this decoder guarantees temporal continuity and reduces high-frequency motion jitter. By smoothing temporal discontinuities from multi-scale fusion, this continuous formulation reduces mechanical execution failures while preserving the base VLA model's generalization and manipulation robustness. Extensive experiments on RoboTwin 2.0 and LIBERO-Plus benchmarks, together with real-world hard evaluations, demonstrate that ActionUNet significantly improves {\pi}0.5 success rates by absolute 9.8%, 6.1%, and 11.4%, respectively, while also generalizing to the regression-based OpenVLA-OFT backbone, highlighting its effectiveness and efficiency as a fine-tuning strategy. Code and implementation details are available at https://github.com/Di-Zhu123/ActionUNet.

2609.35203.title: NucShare: Lightweight Nuclei Instance Segmentation with Foundation-Model Accuracy
2609.35203.authors: Wenyan Li, Xiangyang Jia, Wenlong Zhong, Xu Chen
2609.35203.abstract: Nuclei instance segmentation is fundamental to quantitative pathology. Yet high-accuracy methods mostly build on large vision transformers (ViTs) or heavy convolutional backbones, whose parameter count and compute cost hinder deployment in clinical and edge settings. We present NucShare, a lightweight model whose shared decoder handles nuclear pixel segmentation, horizontal-vertical distance, and classification through learnable transposed convolutions for upsampling and three lightweight heads, using 37% of independent decoders' parameters with no loss in accuracy. Output-level distillation then transfers knowledge from NucShare-T (UNI2-h) to NucShare-S (ConvNeXt V2-Tiny), reducing 690.5M parameters to 34.7M. On PanNuke they reach mPQ 0.524 and 0.519, above the prior best CFR-SAM-H at 0.511, and NucShare-S surpasses HoVer-Net and Mask R-CNN by 5.6 and 15.0 points; on zero-shot MoNuSeg it attains bPQ 0.668 against CFR-SAM-H's 0.662. Code: https://github.com/L-iMeng-L/Newidea

2609.37115.title: NRF-GS: Neural Residual Fields for Expressive and Compact Gaussian Splatting
2609.37115.abstract: We revisit the role of appearance modeling in 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) and show that limited expressiveness in view-dependent reflectance is a key driver of representation redundancy. In standard 3DGS, low-order spherical harmonics (SH) are used, restricting the splats' ability to model high-frequency directional effects, which is typically compensated by increasing the number of splats. We propose \emph{NRF-GS: Neural Residual Fields for Gaussian Splatting}, a hybrid representation that replaces per-splat SH-bases with a shared neural residual field. Each Gaussian encodes a compact set of appearance features and a lambertian base color, while a lightweight \emph{global scene-level MLP} predicts view-dependent residuals conditioned on viewing direction, distance, and per-splat features. This formulation enhances directional reflectance modeling by combining diffuse per-splat reflectance representations with a shared global function for high-frequency details, enabling both higher expressiveness and parameter sharing across splats. Our key insight is that by accurately capturing high-frequency directional reflectance, especially in specular regions, the GS-representation becomes more expressive, reducing the need for geometrically redundant splats. As a result, NRF-GS achieves comparable or better rendering quality while reducing the number of Gaussians by up to 50\%, and produces visibly improved specular and high-frequency details.

2609.38810.title: CRAFT: Causal Responsibility and Failure Tracing in Medical Vision Language Models
2609.38810.authors: Chunzheng Zhu, Jiaqi Zeng, Hongbo Zhao, Yihang Chen, Yijun Wang, Jianxin Lin
2609.38810.abstract: As vision language models are increasingly deployed in clinical diagnosis, understanding how they internally resolve competing visual and textual signals becomes a safety imperative. Existing mechanistic analyses remain confined to unimodal text and offer no explanation for why a single misleading sentence can override a correct image based diagnosis, or why a model commits to a confident answer despite insufficient visual evidence. We find that these two safety risks, arbitration failure where textual context overrides visual grounding and brake failure where the model commits without adequate evidence, are mediated by spatially disjoint attention head populations: arbitration heads form a mid-to-deep wideband reflecting cross-layer evidence competition, while brake heads concentrate in a narrow middle-to-late layer band that regulates evidence sufficiency and abstention behavior. To ground these observations in causal circuitry, we introduce CRAFT, which localizes each failure mode to a minimal causal head set via dual criteria and verifies necessity and sufficiency through temporal probes and Tuned Lens trajectory analysis. Excising arbitration heads sharply reduces conflict following with negligible degradation on clean inputs, while excising brake heads restores appropriate abstention under degraded visual evidence. The two interventions target spatially disjoint head sets and produce distinct corrective effects, underscoring the mechanistic separability of the failure modes. Experiments across multiple medical VQA benchmarks and VLM architectures validate both the localization and interventions, demonstrating that the identified heads causally drive each failure mode and that targeted modulation generalises without retraining. The code is available at https://github.com/zhcz328/CRAFT.

2610.02181.title: OmniSeek: Native Tool Integration for Multi-turn Audio-Visual Reasoning
2610.02181.authors: Haibo Wang, Jiteng Mu, Jialu Li, Jingru Yi, Yuanjun Xiong, Jianming Zhang, Lifu Huang, Mingze Xu
2610.02181.abstract: We present OmniSeek, an agentic framework that transforms an Omni Large Language Model (Omni-LLM) into an active, multi-turn reasoning agent with native tool use. Rather than passively processing an entire audio-visual sequence in a single forward pass, OmniSeek makes evidence acquisition part of the reasoning process: it dynamically decides whether to look or listen, and over which temporal window, to retrieve sparse but critical evidence across different modalities within long contexts. Through an iterative multi-turn protocol, the retrieved raw audio or visual segments are appended back into the context to support subsequent reasoning. To cold-start this capability, we build a data engine that synthesizes OmniTraj-170K, a corpus of multi-hop Chain-of-Thought trajectories with interleaved audio and visual evidence. We first supervise the model on these trajectories to instill multi-turn tool-use behavior, and then further optimize the policy via a two-stage reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. Moreover, we introduce an Audio-Visual Necessity objective that explicitly rewards successful trajectories whose reasoning depends on both modalities, discouraging single-modality shortcuts. Extensive experiments across a wide range of benchmarks demonstrate that OmniSeek learns adaptive cross-modal evidence seeking and consistently improves audio-visual reasoning performance.

2610.05891.title: Spatial Supervision Without Attribution Optimization: Improving Post-Hoc Class Activation Maps via Box-Guided Evidence Routing
2610.05891.authors: Wenhao Liang, Liangwei Nathan Zheng, Lin Yue, Wei Emma Zhang, Mingyu Guo, Weitong Chen
2610.05891.abstract: Post-hoc class activation maps (CAMs) are a standard tool for inspecting the evidence behind an image classifier's predictions, yet nothing in ordinary training encourages these maps to be spatially appropriate. We study whether inexpensive spatial supervision can improve a classifier's own predicted-class Grad-CAM without ever optimizing an attribution map. Box-Guided Evidence Routing (BGER) trains a lightweight gate on the final feature map under box or mask supervision and routes classification through the gated features, while Grad-CAM is computed separately at the pre-gate representation, so the evaluated map never enters the training objective. With a BCE routing loss, BGER raises MaxBoxAccV2 from $0.584$ to $0.715$ on CUB-200-2011 and from $0.757$ to $0.832$ on Stanford Dogs at comparable accuracy. Matched controls attribute most of the ResNet-50 gain to the spatial supervision reshaping the backbone rather than to routing itself: when classification bypasses the gate, most of the improvement remains, and detaching gradients through the gate leaves the ResNet-50 result nearly unchanged. The same detachment preserves most of the gain in two DenseNet-121 chest X-ray settings but removes the apparent gain on Swin-T, and directly supervising the CAM reaches stronger localization at a larger accuracy cost. Overall, spatial supervision can improve separately evaluated post-hoc CAMs, but both the mechanism and the size of the benefit depend on the architecture and the evaluation setting.

2610.07083.title: Graph-Based Recognition of Simulated Train-Driver States From Facial and Upper-Body Keypoints
2610.07083.authors: Olivia Nocentini, Marta Lagomarsino, Gokhan Solak, Younggeol Cho, Qiyi Tong, Sara Zeynalpour, Marta Lorenzini, Alessandro Ledda, Arash Ajoudani
2610.07083.abstract: Driver fatigue poses a significant challenge to railway safety, with traditional systems like the dead-man switch offering limited and basic alertness checks. This study presents a vision-based monitoring system that relies solely on a single front-facing RGB camera and a graph neural network to classify simulated train-driver states into alert, not-alert, and an emergency class comprising acted emergency-like behaviours. To optimize input representations for the model, an ablation study was performed, comparing three feature configurations: skeletal-only, facial-only, and a combination of both. Experimental results show that combining facial and skeletal features yields the highest accuracy (81%) for the three-class model under the light condition, outperforming models that use only facial or skeletal features. Furthermore, the combination of facial and skeletal features achieves 99% accuracy in the alert/not alert classification in light condition. Additionally, we introduced a controlled RGB video dataset containing alert, not alert, and acted emergency-like behaviours recorded under three illumination conditions. These contributions represent a step toward passive and non-contact train-driver state recognition based on facial and upper-body dynamics.

2610.11105.title: TKCAM: Text and Keyframe to Camera Trajectory Generation
2610.11105.authors: Haozhe Yang, Zhiyang Dou, Zekai Gu, Cheng Lin, Wenping Wang, Yuan Liu, Taku Komura
2610.11105.abstract: Generating high-quality and controllable camera motion is essential for AI-assisted cinematography, video synthesis, and 3D scene understanding. We introduce TKCAM, a Text- and Keyframe-conditioned CAMera-motion synthesis framework based on generative masked modeling. We represent camera dynamics using a 12-dimensional kinematic feature comprising position, velocity, and a continuous rotation representation and discretize them into hierarchical motion tokens via a Residual Vector Quantizer (RVQ). A two-stage masked transformer architecture then learns to reconstruct and refine these tokens, utilizing explicit self- and cross-attention modules for multimodal conditioning. A central feature of our framework is sparse visual keyframe conditioning: users can provide free-form text prompts together with RGB observations at selected timestamps, which provide temporally localized visual guidance for generating coherent in-between trajectories. Furthermore, to advance evaluation standards, we curate RealEstate10K-Cap, a large-scale text-camera dataset, and establish a cross-domain benchmark with a Universal CLaTr Evaluator. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TKCAM surpasses recent state-of-the-art baselines on Fr\'echet distance (FID), text-motion matching scores, and retrieval metrics (R@K), while additional analyses evaluate temporal smoothness and cross-domain generalization. Code and RealEstate10K-Cap dataset are available at https://github.com/linearalgebrayhz/TKCAM.

2610.13056.title: A4-MR: Abnormality Aware Anatomical Alignment for MR
2610.13056.authors: Noel D'souza, Zhijian Yang, Nishank Singla, Pranay Doshi, Krisztian Koos, Fei Tan, Bruno Nunes, Laszlo Rusko, Bernadett Kolozsvari, Eszter Sabo, Emanuele Valeriano, Hugh Pemberton, Vikash Gupta, Seyed Iman Zare Estakhraji, Marc Lebel, Farzin Haddadpour, Taha Kass-Hout, Erhan Bas
2610.13056.abstract: Recent advances in large-scale foundation models have enabled strong generalization across a wide range of clinical and research tasks in magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). However, existing vision-language MRI models remain limited in anatomy-specific localization and pathology-aware representation, particularly in real-world settings. We introduce A4-MR, a 3D vision-language foundation model trained on approximately 50,000 MRI studies comprising 491,000 series, roughly half of which are paired with radiology reports. A4-MR is designed to: (1) learn anatomy localization through large-scale pretraining with noisy labels; (2) align image and text representations at the anatomical level; and (3) learn distinct representations of healthy and abnormal anatomy. Across a diverse set of downstream tasks, A4-MR outperforms existing foundation models, including a +1.7 AUROC improvement over MedSigLIP for abnormality detection. Using a frozen encoder, A4-MR also surpasses an end-to-end task-specific MedNeXt model for knee segmentation by +1.4 Dice and performs comparably to the best task-specific model for abdominal organ segmentation on AMOS, within 0.4 Dice. Finally, without anatomical prompts, A4-MR localizes 3D anatomy comparably to MedSAM2 provided with ground-truth bounding boxes. Together, these results demonstrate that anatomy-level multimodal alignment and abnormality-aware representation learning can enable a single MRI foundation model to support localization, segmentation, and pathology-related tasks.

2610.13309.title: NovaSplat: Model-Free 6D Object Pose Estimation via 3D Gaussian Splatting Onboarding and Refinement
2610.13309.authors: Georgios Floros, Evangelos Sartinas, Orestis Vaggelis, Maria Pateraki
2610.13309.abstract: 6D pose estimation of novel objects without CAD models remains an open challenge: model-free methods must build the object representation from scratch during onboarding and have long trailed their model-based counterparts. We present NovaSplat, a model-free pipeline that closes this gap. From a short smartphone video captured at onboarding, we train a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) model that serves both as a template source for detection and coarse pose estimation and as a differentiable backbone for pose refinement. Our refiner optimizes the object-to-camera pose with combined photometric and geometric losses under a continuous rotation parametrization free of gradient singularities. On a household-object benchmark, NovaSplat surpasses all model-based methods. On a challenging industrial benchmark with textureless and specular surfaces, it outperforms all model-free competitors while substantially narrowing the gap to model-based ones. We further introduce NovaSplat-Lite, an inference variant that is $3.1\times$ faster at negligible accuracy cost. Code will be made available at https://github.com/POSE-Lab/novasplat .

2610.18535.title: Meta-Video: Efficient Standardized Evaluation for Video Understanding
2610.18535.authors: Soumya Shamarao Jahagirdar, Anna Kukleva, Vishaal Udandarao, Samuel Thomas, Brian Kingsbury, Rogerio Feris, James R. Glass, Ameya Prabhu, Hilde Kuehne
2610.18535.abstract: Video understanding benchmarks are the primary yardstick for measuring progress in video-language modeling, and a growing body of work relies on them to claim improvements. The reported benchmark scores in these works, however, are almost always produced by frameworks (e.g., lmms eval) used as black boxes: certain evaluation choices like frame sampling, preprocessing, and input formatting are inherited from preset defaults and seldom inspected carefully. We show these unexamined choices are a major source of variance. Even for the same model checkpoint, evaluation configuration alone can shift accuracy by up to 19.5pp. Hence, it is unclear whether reported gains reflect genuine improvements in capability or differences in evaluation setup. Moreover, many benchmark samples offer little evidence of visual capability, since they can be answered without the video, and the full suites are expensive to evaluate. We address these issues in two parts. First, we curate existing suites for discriminability and efficiency, producing Meta-Video, a balanced 1,000-question benchmark over 791 videos spanning diverse tasks and durations, which largely preserves model rankings, at 5 times inference speedup for a full-frame count sweep experiment (4-128 frames). Second, we establish a standardized evaluation protocol by sweeping the configuration space to isolate choices that measurably affect results, distill them into best practices and reporting standards, and release reproducible reference scores across five models and seven benchmarks. We hope that the proposed evaluation framework and the Meta-Video benchmark will support video understanding research by providing a reproducible and efficient foundation to measure progress in a reliable way. Project page: https://soumyasj.github.io/meta-video/

2610.18564.title: Observation Quality in DSM-Assisted Aerial Localization: A Benchmark and Base-Anchored Uncertainty Calibration
2610.18564.authors: Pengyu Yin, Jie Pan, Junxiang Tan, Mengqi Fu, Kun Cheng, Yifan Liu
2610.18564.abstract: Aerial map matching provides position observations for navigation, but a position error alone does not determine how an observation should be weighted. We define five benchmark tasks: position availability and agreement, grouped error structure, predictive uncertainty, controlled updates, and temporal accumulation. We use digital-surface-model-assisted localization to test whether base-anchored uncertainty calibration improves the weighting of unchanged position estimates. The method combines propagated image and map sensitivities with the second moment of a compact configuration subset relative to the reported position. Scale is fitted using separate position references without local surface-height ground truth. Thirteen covariance models are evaluated on two held-out query sets from locations represented in the calibration data. Using reference residuals, we compare the method with a constant full-matrix baseline. With all localization failures included, the method reduces the normalized position-update risk, averaged equally across locations, by 7.70% on 728 conditions and 5.46% on a separate 142 conditions under an independent prior. On the primary set, the equal-location average negative log likelihood on reference residuals improves by 2.571 nat. At these seen locations, exploratory base-only quality calibration and conditional-addition controls leave the incremental update benefit of configuration disagreement unresolved. Navigation benefit and real temporal accumulation remain untested.

2610.23980.title: SituHOI: Scalable Capture of Scene-Situated Full-Body Human-Object Interaction
2610.23980.authors: Qifan Wang, Qihang Fang, Boao Shi, Yushi Du, Pei Zhou, Siyan Dong, Yanchao Yang
2610.23980.abstract: Modeling human-object interaction (HOI) in real environments requires jointly representing whole-body motion, manipulated objects, and scene geometry, yet existing datasets trade off scalable capture against structured, scene-aligned supervision. We introduce SituHOI, a large-scale RGB-D dataset containing 18,429 annotated clips across 16 indoor rooms and approximately 86 hours of quality-screened activity. It pairs recordings from a single moving RGB-D camera with static scene scans, object geometry, language descriptions, and estimated human and object trajectories. Using the scans as persistent references, our pipeline combines camera localization and depth-based metric alignment with human mesh recovery, object tracking, and temporal refinement to register all geometric annotations in a shared floor-aligned frame. These data support FlexHOI-Bench, a goal-conditioned joint motion prediction benchmark with variable observation and prediction durations. Given observed histories, scene and object geometry, and a terminal object pose, models predict future human and object motion. We provide SharedHOI as a reference predictor and evaluate world-space accuracy and human-object coordination. On a MoCap subset, our pipeline reduces human G-MPJPE from 195.4 to 68.3 mm and object translation error from 43.0 to 28.7 mm. SharedHOI leads four adapted baselines on all three aggregate FlexHOI-Bench metrics. Data will be released upon acceptance. An anonymized code repository is available at https://anonymous.4open.science/r/iclr2027-anonymous-code-1DFB.

2610.24005.title: PACE: Pareto-Adaptive Compression for Efficient Native MLLMs
2610.24005.authors: Lei Tian, Chunzheng Zhu, Kai Wu, Yifan Zhang, Haihua Yang
2610.24005.abstract: Native multimodal large language models (native MLLMs) jointly encode visual and linguistic sequences within a unified autoregressive Transformer, emerging as a promising paradigm for multimodal understanding. Unlike conventional ViT-based MLLMs relying on external vision encoders, ViT-free native MLLMs tokenize pixel patches directly, potentially suffering severe visual token redundancy. A pilot study confirms this: unlike ViT-based models that degrade under compression, ViT-free MLLMs tolerate aggressive compression with near-lossless or even improved performance. Yet existing compression methods target ViT-based settings, leaving native MLLMs, which stand to gain the most, unexplored. To close this gap, we introduce an analysis pipeline centered on token discriminability and cross-dimensional heterogeneous redundancy, revealing that (i) redundancy is distributed independently and heterogeneously along height and width axes, and (ii) early-layer visual tokens are indiscriminable and uniformly redundant. Guided by these findings, we propose PACE (Pareto-Adaptive Compression for Efficient Native MLLMs), the first visual token compression framework tailored for native MLLMs with Multimodal-RoPE. Leveraging dimensional decoupling of positional encoding, PACE decomposes attention into two orthogonal spatial saliency estimates along height and width, gated by a positional attention signal, yielding direction-aware importance with negligible overhead. It further casts token budget allocation as Pareto optimization over performance preservation, inference efficiency, and spatial coverage, jointly identifying optimal compression depths and retention ratios. Experiments show PACE maintains near-lossless performance at only 25%-50% visual token retention, even improving several benchmarks, while delivering over 2x FLOPs reduction.

2610.27018.title: PolMamba: Long-wave Infrared Polarimetric Remote Sensing Image Fusion for Vehicle Detection
2610.27018.authors: Wenjuan Zhang, Xiangrui Peng, Zhen Li, Caimeng Yi, Xuesong Ma, Jianwei Wang, Jie Pan
2610.27018.abstract: Blurred vehicle contours and low contrast limit detection performance in infrared remote sensing imagery, while existing fusion methods may introduce polarization noise and fail to integrate complementary information effectively. To address these limitations, we propose a Mamba-based infrared polarimetric remote sensing image fusion model. Infrared polarization information reflects surface material properties and geometry, providing complementary information to infrared intensity. The proposed method first combines long-wave infrared total intensity S0 and the degree of linear polarization (DoLP), using a physics-inspired polarization-response proxy and spatial structural continuity to extract guidance features. It then employs bidirectional state space scanning along horizontal, vertical, and both diagonal orientations to enable cross-modal feature fusion across the entire image. Prior-guided multi-window structural similarity, reconstruction constraints, and a relative lower-bound loss for polarization saliency are jointly introduced to suppress noise while preserving global background structures and target polarization features. In addition, we construct AIR-LWIR-Pol, a dataset of 1,901 accurately registered image pairs acquired using an airborne division-of-aperture long-wave infrared polarimetric imaging system, and evaluate downstream vehicle detection using YOLO11. The experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms the comparison methods on four fusion metrics, including entropy and structural similarity. Vehicle detection mAP50 and mAP50-95 reach 55.0% and 29.4%. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of combining physical priors with state space modeling for long-wave infrared polarization image fusion and support its use for target detection in complex remote sensing scenes.

2610.27049.title: VitronEdit: Universal Visual Editing across Images, Videos, and 3D Scenes
2610.27049.authors: Jing Wang, Yanlin Li, Mong-Li Lee, Wynne Hsu, Shengqiong Wu, Hao Fei
2610.27049.abstract: Recent advances in unified visual editing have begun to consolidate image and video editing within a single model, while 3D scene editing remains largely separate and constrained by scarce paired training data. Given the rich image and video editing supervision now available and the common editing semantics shared across modalities, a natural question is whether this knowledge can be transferred to data-scarce 3D editing. We present VitronEdit, a universal framework for image, video, and 3D scene editing. VitronEdit adopts a shared sequence representation and progressive multimodal training to transfer editing knowledge across modalities. We further introduce geometry-aware post-training, which leverages a pretrained geometry reconstruction model to provide depth and camera-pose supervision. Surprisingly, applying geometric supervision only to 3D samples yields the best overall performance, while image and video editing also improve despite receiving no direct geometric supervision, suggesting that geometric regularization transfers through the shared backbone. Our analysis further shows that image and video training mainly transfers editing semantics to 3D, whereas 3D supervision primarily improves multi-view consistency. The project page: https://vitron-llm.github.io/VitronEdit/.

2610.28195.title: Attractive Faces Skew Text-to-Image Reward Models and Leaderboards
2610.28195.authors: Harvey Mannering, Zhiwu Huang, Adam Pr\"ugel-Bennett
2610.28195.abstract: Human preference is now central to the evaluation, guidance, finetuning, and ranking of text-to-image models. However, the susceptibility of human preferences to bias in image generation remains underexplored. We identify a key observation: for human faces, perceived attractiveness skews image quality judgments, even when comparing real photographs of comparable fidelity. In a controlled user study, annotators rank more attractive faces as higher quality, even when unattractive real faces are compared with attractive AI-generated ones. We examine the downstream consequences of this bias.
